assets.purpose: Transparent reusable logo and game icon
assets.prompt: Use case: logo-brand. Create a new standalone emblem logo for the historical infantry tactics game 'Lions In The Trenches'. Output one emblem ONLY, with no text, on genuine alpha transparency. Design: a powerful, instantly recognizable roaring lion's head in three-quarter profile, its mane expressed as a few bold angular sweeping shapes, embossed in aged gunmetal and weathered brass within an upright hexagonal steel badge. The six-sided badge echoes a tactical hex grid; it has a clean strong silhouette and restrained rivets or edge wear, not a busy coat of arms. The lion face and mane must remain readable when the emblem is displayed at 64 pixels. Use dark charcoal metal recesses, warm tarnished brass highlights, a small amount of bone-ivory edge light, and muted olive oxidation. The mood is determined and battle-worn, appropriate for serious early-to-mid twentieth-century trench infantry, not fantasy. Painted-realistic material finish with subtle scratches, chipped metal and depth, but graphic, disciplined, bold shapes. Center the complete badge on a 1024-by-1024 square canvas with about 10 percent transparent breathing room around all sides. Even front-facing emblem geometry, not a perspective mockup. No background, no rectangular backing plate, no painted checkerboard, no text or initials, no slogan, no crown, no swords, no firearms, no national or political symbols, no skull, no neon or flames, no decorative wreath, no tiny filigree, no watermark. This is the reusable emblem that will be placed between the title lines on the game's splash screen.

assets.purpose: Startup splash with the complete title and new logo
assets.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Asset type: finished square boot splash / key art for the game 'Lions In The Trenches'. Image 1 is the existing splash-screen composition and painterly style reference. Image 2 is the new finished lion emblem to insert faithfully. Create a new, substantially more dynamic version of image 1 with the new logo and the complete title. Preserve the similar square poster setup: a large, compelling infantry soldier in the foreground; rain, smoke and a burning ruined European battlefield behind him; title and badge stacked over his chest and lower body. Preserve the hand-painted watercolor / rough oil illustration style, worn khaki uniform, camouflage-netted Brodie helmet, earthy olive, charcoal, umber and warm orange firelight palette, and the serious human tone of the original. Do not make it a glossy 3D render.
Action: show the main soldier caught in a forceful forward rush out of a muddy trench, torso leaning and twisting, one shoulder advancing, his rifle cutting a strong diagonal across the lower composition, uniform straps and coat tails pulled by movement. His face remains large, clear, human and resolute, above the title. Use wind-slanted rain, mud kicked up by his movement, diagonal drifting smoke, flying embers and a distant shell burst to create a clear sense of kinetic motion. A few small infantry silhouettes moving through the smoke can support the action, without competing with the main figure. Period-appropriate equipment; no modern weapons or modern helmets. No gore.
Branding: replace the old crosshair-and-arrow badge with the NEW LION HEXAGON EMBLEM from image 2. Reproduce its actual lion head, six-sided shape and weathered brass/gunmetal appearance; do not invent another badge or make it part of the soldier's uniform. It is a graphic overlay centered on the lower chest, approximately one fifth of the canvas width. The entire badge must be visible and separate from the lettering. Keep the lion profile distinct and legible.
Text verbatim: 'Lions In The Trenches'. Use exactly these four words and this spelling, no added words or punctuation. Compose the title as the word 'Lions' in one large centered line above the lion badge, and 'In The Trenches' in one strong centered line below it toward the bottom, similar to the original's layout. Use bold, refined military-era slab-serif lettering in pale parchment / worn ivory, with restrained dark shadow or outline so every letter is immediately readable against the painting. The title must not cover the soldier's eyes or face. Keep the complete title safely inset from the edges by at least 6 percent, no clipped letters and no excessively wide tracking. The logo and title must feel like one coherent game identity.
Output: one polished square splash image, aiming for a 2048-by-2048 canvas, full-bleed background with no transparency. More action and movement than the reference, with strong painterly anatomy, a believable rifle grip and no extra fingers. No old emblem, no duplicated title, no slogans, no menu buttons, no UI, no loading bar, no watermark.
